news.title: This college football team just adopted Norway's World Cup Viking Row
news.lede: Norway's Viking Row was one of the most viral fan traditions of the 2026 World Cup. Now, two months later, it has officially made its way into American college football. The University of Minnesota debuted its own version of the synchronized rowing chant at its season opener at Huntington Bank Stadium, with the student section sitting in rows and mimicking the same exaggerated rowing motion that Norwegian fans made famous this summer. Former Gophers linebacker Kamal Martin led the chant before kickoff, keeping one of the World Cup's biggest fan traditions going long after the tournament ended.

news.title: No. 20 Tigers celebrate Memorial Stadium 100th anniversary
news.lede: Mizzou football (2-0, 0-0 SEC) is back at home this week to host Troy (2-0, 0-0 SBC) for the Memorial Stadium 100th anniversary game at 6 p.m. The 20th-ranked team will celebrate the 100th anniversary of Memorial Stadium by wearing special throwback uniforms on the field, according to Mizzou Athletics. The uniforms will bring back Tiger nostalgia, combining elements from several areas of Mizzou football including the 1920's-style "M' on the jersey, 1970's-inspired sleeve stripes and a narrow Block M with a gray facemask reminiscent of the helmet design introduced in 1971, according to Mizzou Athletics. The helmets front bumper will display the six Columns of Francis Quadrangle, while the pants will represent the historic shade of gold worn by the Tigers through the 20th century, according to Mizzou Athletics.

news.title: Morocco international Khalid Boutaib announces retirement from football
news.lede: Former Morocco international Khalid Boutaib announced Saturday that he is retiring from professional football, bringing an end to a career that saw him represent the national team at the 2018 FIFA World Cup in Russia. Boutaib reflected on his career in an emotional message shared on social media, recalling how he spent several years playing amateur football while pursuing his studies. In his farewell message, Boutaib thanked his family, friends, coaches, teammates, technical staff and supporters who accompanied him throughout his career.

news.title: Italian football mourns Inter legend Mazzola
news.lede: Inter and Italy legend Sandro Mazzola has passed away at the age of 83 after a long illness. Son of Valentino Mazzola, the legendary leader of the great Torino side who perished in the Superga air disaster in 1949, Sandro joined Inter as a young boy, playing his whole career with the Nerazzurri and contributing to the success of the "Grande Inter". Mazzola was the embodiment of Helenio Herrera’s legendary side, playing a pivotal role in the team's first major European Cup triumph against Real Madrid in 1964. In total, he won four league titles, two European Cups, and two Intercontinental Cups, appearing 417 times and scoring 116 goals.

news.title: 'We never gave up, and that's the best message we could send': Scaloni looks beyond tough World Cup
news.lede: Lionel Scaloni believes Argentina’s run to the 2026 World Cup final demanded more from his team than their previous triumph in Qatar, with injuries and fitness issues forcing difficult decisions along the way. Now, with the tournament behind them, the Argentina coach wants to use the next phase to introduce younger players without losing the spirit that has carried the team through an extraordinary eight-year cycle. Speaking to Asian channel MiGu, Scaloni revealed that Argentina arrived in the United States in considerably worse physical condition than they had in Qatar. “We arrived at the previous World Cup (2022) in much better shape, with 95% of the players at their best; this time we arrived with just enough,” Scaloni said.

news.title: Russia handed partial international football return as FIFA includes youth team in Under-15 World Cup draw
news.lede: Youth squad enters tournamentRussia have officially returned to the international football fold at youth level after being included in the group-stage draw for the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan. Placed in a six-team pool alongside Turkey, Afghanistan, Djibouti, Sierra Leone, and Sudan, the decision marks the first easing of sporting sanctions against the nation since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Explaining the central purpose behind launching the pilot competition, FIFA stated: "The FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival addresses a fundamental challenge in international football: providing meaningful competitive opportunities for nations in which qualifying for FIFA competitions remains an enormous challenge."
